title: Criminal Lawyer Advertising: Where to Spend | CaseAuthority
meta: Criminal lawyer advertising explained for defense attorneys: Google Ads, Local Services Ads, the map, social, TV, radio and billboards, ad rules and what to track.
h1: Criminal Lawyer Advertising: Where Defense Firms Should Spend
lead: Most people who need a criminal defense lawyer did not plan to need one. An arrest, a court date in the mail or a call from a detective sends them looking for help fast, often late at night and often on their phone. Criminal lawyer advertising is about being in front of those people at that moment, with a message that makes them feel safe calling you. This guide walks criminal defense attorneys through the main advertising channels, how each one fits the way people look for a defense lawyer, the advertising rules to keep in mind, the busy seasons in criminal defense, and how to tell which ads are bringing you real clients.
quick_answer: Criminal lawyer advertising is any paid way of getting your defense firm in front of people who have been arrested or charged. The most common channels are Google search ads, Google Local Services Ads, paid placement around the map results, social media ads, and traditional media such as TV, radio, billboards and bus benches. Because criminal cases are urgent and local, ads that appear right when someone searches, and that lead to a phone answered by a person, usually work best. Every ad must follow your state bar's lawyer advertising rules, and every channel should be judged by signed clients, not clicks.
takeaways: People look for a defense lawyer soon after an arrest. Be visible and easy to reach at that moment.
Google ads and Local Services Ads appear when someone is actively looking for help.
Ads for DUI, drug charges, assault or theft usually beat a general criminal lawyer message.
TV, radio and billboards help people remember your name when they need it.
Lawyer advertising rules vary by state. Avoid promises and guarantees.
Judge every channel by retained clients and fees, not clicks or impressions.

sections.answer: It is any paid way of putting your defense firm in front of people who have been arrested, charged or are under investigation.
paras: Advertising is different from the free ways people find a lawyer, such as word of mouth, your website ranking in Google or your Google Business Profile showing in the map. With advertising you pay to be seen, either per click, per lead, or for a block of airtime or space.

For criminal defense firms, advertising has a special job. Your future clients are often scared, embarrassed and in a hurry. Many have never spoken to a lawyer before. A good ad tells them three things very quickly: you handle their kind of case, you are close by, and they can talk to someone now.

Criminal defense advertising usually works alongside other marketing, not instead of it. Ads can bring calls quickly, while your website, reviews and local search visibility keep working when the ads are turned off. You can read more about the wider picture in our guide to [[a:criminal-defense-marketing|criminal defense marketing]].

sections.h2: How Do People Look for a Criminal Defense Lawyer?
sections.answer: Most search on their phone soon after an arrest or court notice, look at the first few results, and call the firm that seems ready to help.
paras: Many people search within hours of being released, or as soon as they find a court date in their paperwork. Family members often search on their behalf. Searches tend to be specific, for example a DUI lawyer near me, a drug possession lawyer in a certain county, or a lawyer for a first offense.
People in this situation do not compare a dozen firms. They usually look at the ads and the map results at the top, check a few reviews and call. If nobody answers, they call the next firm.

This tells you a lot about where to advertise. Channels that show up at the moment of need, such as search ads, tend to bring the most urgent calls. Channels that build familiarity over time, such as radio or billboards, help people remember your name when the moment comes. Both depend on what happens when the phone rings.

sections.h2: Do Google Ads Work for Criminal Defense Lawyers?
sections.answer: They can work very well because they appear at the moment someone searches, but clicks are often expensive, so careful setup matters.
paras: Google search ads let your firm appear at the top of the results for searches you choose, such as criminal defense lawyer plus your city, or DUI attorney near me. You pay when someone clicks. Because many defense firms bid on the same searches, the cost per click in criminal defense can be high, especially in large cities.

The firms that get the most out of Google Ads usually keep their campaigns tightly focused. They run separate ads for each main charge type, limit ads to the areas they actually serve, run ads at the times their phones are answered, and send each ad to a page that matches it. An ad for DUI defense should lead to a DUI page, not your home page.

It also helps to block searches that will never become clients, such as searches for free legal aid, jobs at law firms or general information about the law. Reviewing the search terms report regularly keeps budget focused on people who need a lawyer.

sections.h2: Are Google Local Services Ads Worth It for Criminal Defense?
sections.answer: For many defense firms, yes. Local Services Ads appear above other results and you pay per lead rather than per click, but you need screening and good reviews.
paras: Google Local Services Ads show a small set of firms at the very top of many local searches, with a badge, a star rating and a call button. For lawyers, Google screens the firm before the ads go live, which can add trust.

You pay for leads, usually calls or messages, rather than clicks. That can make costs easier to predict, but you still need to dispute leads that are clearly not relevant, and you need a fast, friendly response to every call. Reviews have a strong effect on how often your ad is shown, so a steady flow of genuine reviews helps.
Local Services Ads are only available for certain practice areas and locations, and the rules and categories change from time to time, so check what is available in your area.

sections.h2: What About the Map Results and Your Google Business Profile?
sections.answer: The map results are not ads, but they sit right next to them. A strong Google Business Profile makes every ad you run work harder.
paras: When someone searches for a criminal lawyer near them, Google often shows a map with three firms below the ads. Being in that map is earned, not bought, through a complete and accurate Google Business Profile, the right categories, steady reviews and a website that backs it up.

This matters for advertising because people compare. If they see your ad, then see your firm in the map with good reviews, they are more likely to call. If your ad appears but your profile looks empty, they may choose someone else. Our guide to [[a:local-seo-for-criminal-defense-lawyers|local SEO for criminal defense lawyers]] explains how the map works in more detail.

sections.h2: Should Criminal Defense Firms Advertise on Social Media?
sections.answer: Social media ads rarely catch someone at the moment of arrest, but they can build awareness and keep your name in front of past contacts.
paras: People do not usually open Facebook or Instagram to look for a defense lawyer after an arrest. That makes social media ads less direct than search ads for criminal defense. They are better suited to building familiarity in your area, promoting helpful content such as what to do after a DUI arrest, and reaching people who have already visited your website.

Short videos of an attorney explaining a common question in plain words can work well, because they show a real person people can trust. Keep the tone calm and respectful. Ads that make fun of people's situations or use fear can damage your reputation and may break advertising rules.
Social media platforms also have their own rules for legal ads and for targeting, so check them before you launch a campaign.

sections.h2: Do TV, Radio and Billboards Still Work for Criminal Lawyers?
sections.answer: They can, especially in markets where a firm wants to be the name people remember, but they cost more and are harder to track.
paras: Traditional advertising builds name recognition. Someone who has heard your name on the radio for months, or driven past your billboard every day, may search for you by name when they or a family member get into trouble. Some firms also use bus benches and signs near courthouses and jails, where local rules allow it.

The challenge is cost and measurement. TV and billboards usually need a large budget and a long commitment to work. It is also harder to know exactly which calls came from them. Using a dedicated phone number or a simple web address for each campaign, and asking every new caller how they heard about you, helps.

For many smaller defense firms, search ads, Local Services Ads and a strong local presence come first. Traditional media often makes more sense once those are working and the firm wants to grow its brand in a wider area.

sections.h2: Should You Advertise by Charge Type?
sections.answer: Usually yes. Ads that name a specific charge, such as DUI, drug possession or domestic violence, tend to connect better than a general message.
paras: Someone charged with a DUI wants a DUI lawyer. Someone accused of domestic violence wants a lawyer who understands those cases. Ads that speak directly to the charge, and lead to a page about that charge in your area, usually get more calls and better clients than a general criminal defense ad.

Start with the charges that make up most of your work, or the ones you most want more of. Then make sure each one has its own clear page on your website. Our post on [[a:blog/dui-lawyer-seo|DUI lawyer SEO]] explains why separate pages for each case type help both ads and search results.
Use the words your state uses. If your state calls it DWI or OWI, your ads and pages should too.

sections.h2: When Are the Busy Seasons in Criminal Defense Advertising?
sections.answer: Arrests and searches tend to rise around holidays, summer and big local events, so plan budgets and staffing ahead of those periods.
paras: Many areas see more DUI enforcement around holidays such as Thanksgiving, the end of the year, the Fourth of July and Labor Day, as well as around large local events and college term dates. Searches for defense lawyers often rise around the same times.

Planning ahead helps. Increase budgets and make sure your phones are covered evenings and weekends before these periods start, not after. Check last year's call records to see when your own busy times were, because every market is a little different.
Quieter months are a good time to improve your website, collect reviews and test new ads, so you are ready when demand rises again.

sections.h2: What Are the Advertising Rules for Criminal Defense Lawyers?
sections.answer: Your ads must follow your state bar's lawyer advertising rules. Avoid guarantees, misleading claims and anything that could identify a client without consent.
paras: Every state regulates lawyer advertising, and the rules differ. Common themes include not making false or misleading claims, not promising results, being careful with words like expert or specialist, including required disclaimers and labeling ads as attorney advertising where required.

Criminal defense has some extra sensitivities. Talking about past case results can be restricted, and you should never share details that could identify a client without proper consent. Some states also limit contacting people directly after an arrest, for example through mailers based on arrest records, or set waiting periods before you can do so.
Before launching a new campaign, check your state bar's rules and any ethics opinions that apply, and keep copies of your ads in case you are ever asked about them.

sections.h2: What Happens After Someone Clicks or Calls?
sections.answer: The response decides whether advertising pays off. Answer every call live, reply to forms in minutes and treat every caller with respect.
paras: Advertising only brings the opportunity. The case is won or lost on the phone. People who have just been arrested often call several firms. The first firm that answers kindly, explains the next steps and offers a clear consultation is usually the one they hire.

Make sure calls are answered live during the hours your ads run, including evenings and weekends if you advertise then. Reply to web forms and chat messages within minutes. Keep a short, friendly script that covers the charge, the court date, the location and how to book a consultation.
Review a sample of calls regularly. If good callers are not booking, the fix may be in how calls are handled, not in the ads.

sections.h2: How Do You Know Which Ads Are Bringing Clients?
sections.answer: Track each inquiry from first contact to retained client and fee, then compare that with what each channel cost.
paras: Use call tracking numbers for each channel, connect your ad accounts to conversion tracking, and ask every new caller how they found you. Record the source of each inquiry next to whether it booked a consultation, whether the person hired you and the fee.

With that information you can work out the cost per retained client for each channel. A channel that brings fewer calls but more hires may be worth more than one that brings lots of calls that go nowhere.
Review the numbers monthly and adjust. Move budget toward the channels and charge types that bring retained clients, and pause the ones that do not.

sections.answer: This is general information for criminal defense firms, not legal, ethics or compliance advice.
paras: Any examples of how ads, costs, seasons or results tend to work are general and for illustration only. They are not promises of results for your firm. Results vary by city, competition, budget, reviews, website, intake and the work done.

Rules on lawyer advertising, client confidentiality, case results and contacting people after an arrest vary by state and change over time. Check your state bar's rules before launching or changing any advertising.

faq.q: What Is the Best Way to Advertise as a Criminal Defense Lawyer?
faq.a: For many firms, the best starting point is Google search ads and Local Services Ads, because they appear when people are actively looking, backed by a strong Google Business Profile and fast, friendly call handling. TV, radio and billboards can add brand recognition once the basics work.

faq.q: How Much Should a Criminal Defense Firm Spend on Advertising?
faq.a: There is no single right amount. It depends on your city, competition, case types and goals. Start with a budget you can sustain, track cost per retained client closely, and increase spending on the channels that prove they bring clients.

faq.q: Can Criminal Defense Lawyers Advertise on Facebook?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the ads follow your state bar rules and the platform's own rules for legal services. Facebook ads usually work better for awareness and helpful content than for catching someone right after an arrest.

faq.q: Are Local Services Ads Good for Criminal Defense?
faq.a: For many defense firms they are, because they appear at the top of local searches and charge per lead. Good reviews and fast responses make a big difference to how well they work.

faq.q: Can I Advertise Past Case Results?
faq.a: It depends on your state. Many states allow it with conditions, such as disclaimers that past results do not guarantee future outcomes, while some restrict it more. Never share details that could identify a client without proper consent.

faq.q: Is Advertising Better Than SEO for Criminal Lawyers?
faq.a: They do different jobs. Advertising brings calls quickly but stops when spending stops. SEO takes longer to build but keeps bringing calls without paying for each click. Most growing defense firms use both.
